exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Overly permissive default rules can allow attackers to bridge network boundaries that should be segmented, bypassing intended security controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: Permissive default rulesets may allow tunneling protocols that would otherwise be blocked, enabling covert communications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposed management interfaces provide remote service access points that attackers can exploit to gain unauthorized access to network devices.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Network Device Firewall
exploitedBy.relevance: Network-exposed management interfaces can be leveraged to disable or modify firewall rules on network devices.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Password Guessing
exploitedBy.relevance: Default or weak credentials are highly susceptible to password guessing attacks against management interfaces.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Valid Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or default credentials enable attackers to gain access using valid account credentials without sophisticated techniques.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credential Stuffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Default credentials are commonly included in credential stuffing lists, making devices with unchanged defaults easy targets.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Log Enumeration
exploitedBy.relevance: The absence of rule logging means adversaries can operate without generating audit evidence that defenders could enumerate.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted management channels expose credentials and configuration data to network sniffing attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted management protocols can be abused or intercepted to facilitate data exfiltration over cleartext channels.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Stale firmware and software versions contain known vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to compromise public-facing network devices.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Patch System Image
exploitedBy.relevance: Outdated firmware creates opportunities for attackers to replace or modify the system image with compromised versions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Email Hiding Rules
exploitedBy.relevance: Redundant and shadowed rules can obscure malicious rules inserted by attackers, analogous to hiding rules that mask attacker activity.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Traffic Signaling
exploitedBy.relevance: Shadowed or redundant firewall rules may inadvertently allow traffic signaling techniques that would otherwise be blocked by correct rule ordering.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing egress filtering allows unrestricted data exfiltration to external web services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Absent egress filtering enables exfiltration over unencrypted protocols without interception or blocking.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
exploitedBy.relevance: Without MFA enforcement, attackers do not need to bypass MFA challenges to gain administrative access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
exploitedBy.relevance: The absence of MFA on admin access directly relates to MFA bypass techniques used to gain unauthorized privileged access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Interception
exploitedBy.relevance: When MFA is absent, attackers face no MFA interception challenge, making admin account compromise significantly easier.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Device Configuration Dump
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted configuration backups can be dumped and read by attackers to extract sensitive network device configurations.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted configuration backup files often contain credentials that attackers can extract directly.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Private Keys
exploitedBy.relevance: Unsigned and unencrypted backups may expose private keys stored in configuration files.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Indicator Blocking
exploitedBy.relevance: Misconfigured log forwarding prevents security indicators from reaching SIEM or monitoring systems, effectively blocking detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
exploitedBy.relevance: Absent log forwarding means attacker activity that would be detected via centralized logs goes unnoticed, similar to clearing logs.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Account Manipulation
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive privilege assignment enables attackers who compromise any admin account to manipulate other accounts with broad permissions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive privilege assignment in cloud environments can be abused through temporary elevated access mechanisms.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Non-Application Layer Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Without stateful inspection, non-application layer protocol abuse for C2 communications cannot be properly detected or blocked.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote System Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposed ICMP services enable attackers to perform remote system discovery and network mapping.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: SNMP (MIB Dump)
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposed diagnostic services including SNMP allow attackers to dump MIB data and gather extensive network configuration information.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: ICMP and diagnostic service overexposure enables attackers to discover network configuration and topology details.
